p.src: Now Wu Song had pinned Jiang the Gatekeeper to the ground. He said, “If you want me to spare your life, you need only agree to three conditions!” Jiang the Gatekeeper said, “Name them, good sir. I, Jiang Zhong, will agree to them all.” Wu Song said, “First, you must leave the Happy Grove at once and immediately return all its furnishings and property to their original owner, Shi En, the Golden-Eyed Tiger. Who gave you the right to seize it from him by force?” Jiang the Gatekeeper hurriedly replied, “I agree, I agree.” Wu Song said, “Second, once I let you get up, you are to invite all the leading heroes and worthies of the Happy Grove to come and apologize to Shi En on your behalf.” Jiang the Gatekeeper said, “I will agree to that too.” Wu Song said, “Third, after you have handed everything back today, you must leave the Happy Grove and return to your native place tonight. You are not permitted to remain in Mengzhou! If you stay here instead of leaving, every time I see you, I will beat you once; if I see you ten times, I will beat you ten times. At the least I will beat you half dead; at the worst I will finish you off. Do you agree?” Hearing this, Jiang the Gatekeeper, desperate to save his life, repeatedly answered, “I agree, I agree! I, Jiang Zhong, agree to everything.” Wu Song hauled Jiang the Gatekeeper up from the ground. His face was bruised and his mouth swollen, his neck twisted to one side, and fresh blood streamed from his temple. Pointing at Jiang the Gatekeeper, Wu Song said, “Never mind a stupid brute like you! Even the great tiger on Jingyang Ridge took me only a few punches and kicks to kill! What is the likes of you worth? Hurry and return everything to him! Delay even a little and you will get another beating—one that will finish you for good!” Only then did Jiang the Gatekeeper realize that this was Wu Song. He could do nothing but assent over and over and beg for mercy. While they were speaking, Shi En arrived with twenty or thirty fierce and stalwart soldiers who had all come to lend their aid. When they saw that Wu Song had defeated Jiang the Gatekeeper, they were overjoyed and crowded around him. Pointing at Jiang the Gatekeeper, Wu Song said, “The rightful owner is here now. Start moving your things at once, and hurry to invite people here to speak in apology for you.” Jiang the Gatekeeper replied, “Good sir, please come into the tavern and be seated first.”

p.src: Wu Song led the whole party into the tavern, where they found wine spilled all over the floor. The wretched man and woman were still in the vats, struggling to their feet by groping along the walls. The woman had only just managed to crawl out of a vat. Her head and face had been gashed by the knocks, while her lower body was drenched and dripping with wine. The tavern hands and servers had fled without a trace.

p.src: Wu Song entered the tavern with the others and sat down. He shouted, “Pack up quickly and be on your way!” They arranged a cart and packed the baggage, sending the woman away first. At the same time, an uninjured server was sent into town to invite more than ten of its leading worthies to the tavern, there to apologize to Shi En on Jiang the Gatekeeper’s behalf. They opened as much fine wine as anyone could drink, set out all the plentiful dishes to accompany it, and invited everyone to take a seat. Wu Song had Shi En sit in the place of honor above Jiang the Gatekeeper. A large bowl was placed before each man, and the attendants were told to keep pouring wine without pause.

p.src: After several bowls of wine, Wu Song began to speak: “Honored neighbors, since you are all gathered here, let me explain. I am Wu Song. Ever since I killed a man in Yanggu County and was exiled here, I have heard people say, ‘This tavern in the Happy Grove, together with its buildings and businesses, was originally the property of young Prison Warden Shi. But Jiang the Gatekeeper relied on powerful backing and brazenly seized them, taking away the man’s livelihood for nothing.’ Do not suppose that he is my master; there is no such connection between us. I have always made it my business to strike down such men in this world who have neither justice nor virtue. Whenever I encounter injustice on the road, I truly draw my blade to help, and I do not fear even death. Today I had meant to beat this fellow Jiang to death with my fists and feet and rid the world of a pest. Out of respect for all you good neighbors, I will temporarily leave this fellow his life. But he must leave for another prefecture tonight. If he does not leave this place and I encounter him again, the tiger on Jingyang Ridge will show what his fate shall be.” Only then did everyone realize that he was Constable Wu, the tiger-slayer of Jingyang Ridge. They all rose and pleaded on Jiang the Gatekeeper’s behalf: “Good sir, calm your anger. We will make him move away at once and return everything to its rightful owner.” Jiang the Gatekeeper had been so terrified by Wu Song that he did not dare utter another word. Shi En took an inventory of the furnishings and property and formally took possession of the tavern. His face covered with shame, Jiang the Gatekeeper thanked everyone, summoned a cart himself, loaded his baggage, and departed. Nothing more need be said of that.

p.src: Now Wu Song invited all the honored neighbors to drink, and they did not stop until they were thoroughly drunk. When evening came, the guests dispersed. Wu Song slept soundly and did not wake until the hour of the dragon the following morning. Meanwhile, when old Prison Warden Shi heard that his son Shi En had regained control of the Happy Grove tavern, he rode straight there to thank Wu Song and spent several successive days drinking in celebration at the tavern. Everyone throughout the Happy Grove learned how formidable Wu Song was, and there was not one who did not come to pay his respects. Thereafter they put the premises in order again and reopened the tavern, while the old prison warden returned to Anping Stockade to attend to his duties. Shi En sent men to inquire after Jiang the Gatekeeper, but though he had taken his entire household with him, no one knew where he had gone. Here they simply carried on with their own business and paid him no further heed, while Wu Song remained living at the tavern. From then on, Shi En’s business earned thirty to fifty percent more profit than before, while all the other taverns, gambling houses, and exchange houses doubled their payments of tribute money to him. Because Wu Song had vindicated him, Shi En respected and cherished Wu Song as though he were his own father and mother. Thus Shi En regained dominion over the Happy Grove on the Mengzhou road. Nothing further need be said of it. Indeed:

p.src: As time slipped quietly by, more than a month soon passed. The fierce heat gradually receded; jeweled dew brought coolness, and autumn winds drove away the summer heat. Deep autumn had arrived. Where there is something to tell, the tale is long; where there is nothing, it is brief. That day, Shi En and Wu Song were sitting idly in the tavern, discussing boxing, staff fighting, and spear techniques, when two or three soldiers appeared before the door leading a horse. They entered and asked the proprietor, “Which man is Constable Wu, the tiger slayer?” Shi En recognized them as personal attendants from the yamen of Zhang Mengfang, the military commandant responsible for the defense of Mengzhou. Shi En stepped forward and asked, “What business have you with Constable Wu?” One of the soldiers replied, “By His Excellency the Commandant’s order. He has heard that Constable Wu is a fine man, and specially sent us with this horse to fetch him. Here is His Excellency’s summons.” Shi En read it and thought, “Commandant Zhang is my father’s superior officer, and my father is subject to his orders; and now Wu Song is also a transported prisoner under his jurisdiction. I have no choice but to let him go.” Shi En then said to Wu Song, “Elder brother, these gentlemen have been sent by His Excellency Commandant Zhang to fetch you. Since he has even sent men with a horse, what do you think?” Wu Song was a straightforward man who knew nothing of cautious maneuvering. He said at once, “Since he has summoned me, I must make the journey and hear what he has to say.” He immediately changed his clothes and headcloth, took a young attendant with him, mounted the horse, and accompanied the men toward the city of Mengzhou.

p.src: When they reached Commandant Zhang’s residence, Wu Song dismounted and followed the soldier straight to the hall, where he was presented to Commandant Zhang. Zhang Mengfang was seated in the hall. Delighted to see Wu Song arrive, he said, “Have him come forward and greet me.” Wu Song came below the hall, bowed to Commandant Zhang, then stood to one side with hands clasped. Commandant Zhang said to him, “I have heard that you are a true man and stout fellow, an invincible hero who dares share life and death with others. I happen to lack such a man in my personal retinue. Would you be willing to serve as my trusted attendant?” Wu Song knelt and thanked him, saying, “This humble man is merely a prisoner in the prison camp. If Your Excellency should favor and advance me, I shall hold your whip and follow your stirrup, devoting myself to your service.” Commandant Zhang was overjoyed and ordered fruit and wine to be brought. He personally offered Wu Song wine and had him drink until he was thoroughly drunk. He had a side room beneath the front hall gallery put in order for Wu Song to sleep in. The next day he sent men to Shi En’s place to fetch Wu Song’s luggage, and from then on Wu Song lodged in Commandant Zhang’s residence. Morning and evening, His Excellency the Commandant repeatedly summoned Wu Song into the rear hall and gave him food and wine. He allowed him free passage through the inner rooms and treated him like one of the family; he also ordered a tailor to make Wu Song a complete set of autumn clothes, from inner garments to outer robes. Wu Song was pleased by all this and thought, “It is rare indeed to find a commandant so determined to advance me. Ever since I came to live here, I have scarcely left his side and have had no time to go to the Forest of Delight and speak with Shi En. Though he frequently sends people to inquire after me, in all likelihood he cannot gain entry into this residence. …”

The cries of newly arrived wild geese were mournful; the notes of cold crickets rang urgently. Autumn stood at its midpoint as the seasons turned; a perfectly round moon shone over mountains and rivers.

p.src: At that time, Commandant Zhang had a banquet prepared beneath the Mandarin Ducks Tower deep within the rear hall to celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival, and summoned Wu Song inside to drink. When Wu Song saw the commandant’s wife and the other women of the household seated at the feast, he drank one cup and made to turn and leave. Commandant Zhang called him back and asked, “Where are you going?” Wu Song replied, “Your Excellency, your lady and the women of your household are feasting here. It is only proper that this humble man withdraw.” Commandant Zhang laughed heartily. “You are mistaken. I esteem you as a man of honor and specially invited you to drink together with us, just as if you were family. Why should you withdraw?” He then ordered Wu Song to sit. Wu Song said, “This humble man is a prisoner. How could I dare sit beside Your Excellency?” Commandant Zhang said, “Worthy sir, why do you treat us as strangers? There are no outsiders here. There is no harm in sitting down.” Again and again Wu Song modestly declined and begged leave to go, but Commandant Zhang would not release him and insisted that he sit with them. Wu Song had no choice but to salute and apologize for his discourtesy, then sat far off to one side, his body turned at an angle. Commandant Zhang had the maidservants and serving women urge him to drink. Cup followed cup, and before long Wu Song had drunk five or seven. Commandant Zhang ordered a fruit table brought up and continued drinking with him. After another course or two of food, they chatted idly and discussed some spear techniques. Commandant Zhang said, “When a true man drinks, what use has he for little cups?” He ordered a large silver presentation goblet to be brought and filled with wine for the worthy hero. p.src: When did the bright moon first appear? Raising my wine, I ask the azure sky: In the celestial palace above, what year is this very night? I would ride the wind and return there, but fear those jeweled towers and jade halls, where the heights are too cold to endure. I rise and dance, playing with my clear shadow—yet how could that compare with the mortal world? It passes the high-rolled pearl blinds, shines low through carved windows, and illumines the sleepless. Surely the moon bears no grudge—why, then, is it always full when people are parted? People know sorrow and joy, parting and reunion; the moon has darkness and brightness, fullness and waning. Since ancient times, such things have never been complete. May those dear to us live long, and though ten thousand miles apart, share the beauty of this moon.

p.src: When Yulan had finished singing, she laid down the ivory clappers, curtsied once more to each of them, and stood to one side. Commandant Zhang then said, “Yulan, serve another round of wine.” Yulan obeyed and took up a serving tray. A maid poured the wine; Yulan first offered a cup to the commandant, next to his wife, and third urged Wu Song to drink. Commandant Zhang ordered the cup filled to the brim. Wu Song dared not even raise his head. He rose and received the wine from a respectful distance, bowed deeply to the commandant and his wife, then lifted the cup, drained it at one draught, and returned it. Pointing to Yulan, Commandant Zhang said to Wu Song, “This girl is quite clever and quick-witted. She understands music well and is highly skilled with her needle. If you do not disdain her humble station, within a few days I shall choose an auspicious hour and give her to you as your wife.” Wu Song rose and bowed twice. “What sort of man am I, that I should dare hope to take a member of my benefactor’s household as my wife? It would only be a waste of fodder on a brute like Wu Song.” Commandant Zhang laughed. “Since I have said it, I am determined to give her to you. Do not invent excuses to refuse me. I shall certainly keep my word.”

Wu Song dared not even raise his head. He rose and received the wine from a respectful distance, bowed deeply to the commandant and his wife, then lifted the cup, drained it at one draught, and returned it.
Pointing to Yulan, Commandant Zhang said to Wu Song, “This girl is quite clever and quick-witted. She understands music well and is highly skilled with her needle.
If you do not disdain her humble station, within a few days I shall choose an auspicious hour and give her to you as your wife.”
Wu Song rose and bowed twice. “What sort of man am I, that I should dare hope to take a member of my benefactor’s household as my wife?
It would only be a waste of fodder on a brute like Wu Song.”
Commandant Zhang laughed. “Since I have said it, I am determined to give her to you.
Do not invent excuses to refuse me. I shall certainly keep my word.”

p.src: They went on to drink more than a dozen cups. When Wu Song felt the wine rising, he feared he might forget his manners. He therefore rose, thanked the commandant and his wife, and withdrew to the door of his room beneath the front hall veranda. He opened the door, but with wine and food heavy in his belly he could not sleep at once. He entered, took off his outer clothes and headcloth, then carried his staff into the middle of the hall. Beneath the bright moon he practised several bouts with it and executed a few whirling movements; looking up at the sky, he judged it to be around the third watch. Wu Song returned to his room and was just about to undress and sleep when a great cry arose in the rear quarters: “Thieves!” Hearing it, Wu Song thought, “The commandant treats me with such kindness. How can I fail to protect him when a thief has entered his inner quarters?” Eager to prove his devotion, Wu Song seized his staff and rushed straight into the rear quarters. There he saw Yulan, the singer, hurrying out in alarm and pointing. “A thief has fled into the rear garden!” At these words Wu Song strode straight into the garden with his staff and searched all around, but found no one. He turned and hurried back, but without warning a bench was thrust from the darkness and tripped him headlong. Seven or eight soldiers rushed out, shouting, “Catch the thief!” They bound Wu Song on the ground with a hempen rope. Wu Song cried urgently, “It is I!” But the soldiers would not let him explain. The hall was ablaze with lamps and candles. Commandant Zhang sat there, repeatedly shouting, “Bring him in!” The soldiers drove Wu Song to the hall, striking him at every step. Wu Song shouted, “I am no thief! I am Wu Song!” At the sight of him, Commandant Zhang flew into a rage. His face changed and he cursed, “You thieving convict! You were a bandit from the start, a man with a thief’s heart and guts. I meant to raise you up and make a man of you, and never treated you badly in the least. Only just now I had you drink with us and sit at our own table. I intended to advance you and obtain an office for you—how could you commit such a deed?” Wu Song cried, “My lord, I had nothing to do with it! I came to catch the thief. Why have you arrested me as the thief instead? Wu Song is an upright hero and would never do such a thing.” Commandant Zhang roared, “Do not try to deny it, you wretch! Take him to his room and search it for stolen goods.” The soldiers marched Wu Song straight to his room. When they opened his wicker trunk, they found clothes on top, but beneath them lay silver wine vessels—some one or two hundred taels’ worth of stolen goods. At the sight, even Wu Song stared dumbfounded, able only to protest his innocence. The soldiers carried the trunk before the hall. Commandant Zhang looked at it and cursed, “You thieving convict, what insolence! The stolen goods were found in your own trunk—how can you possibly deny it? As the saying goes, ‘All creatures may be saved, but a man is hard to save!’ So beneath your human appearance you have the heart and guts of a thief. The stolen goods are here and the evidence is plain. There is nothing more to say.” That very night he had the stolen goods sealed and sent to the confidential office for safekeeping, saying he would deal with the wretch at daybreak. Wu Song loudly protested his innocence, but no one would hear his explanation. The soldiers carried away the stolen goods and took Wu Song to be held in the confidential office. During the night Commandant Zhang sent a man to report the matter to the prefect, and money was passed to all the clerks and judicial officers, high and low.

p.src: At daybreak the next morning, when the prefect had just taken his seat in court, the arresting officers brought Wu Song before him, with all the stolen goods carried into the hall. A trusted man from Commandant Zhang’s household brought the commandant’s written report of the theft and presented it to the prefect. The prefect ordered his attendants to bind Wu Song and throw him down. The jailers and warders placed a bundle of instruments of interrogation before him. Wu Song was about to explain when the prefect shouted, “This wretch was already a convict sentenced to distant exile. How could he not turn thief? He must have been suddenly tempted at the sight of wealth. Since the stolen goods and evidence are conclusive, do not listen to his nonsense. Beat him with all your strength!” The jailers and guards raised their flat bamboo rods and brought them down like pelting rain. Wu Song realized that reason was useless and had no choice but to make a false confession: “On the fifteenth day of this month, I saw many silver wine vessels in my master’s residence and was suddenly tempted. That night I seized the opportunity to steal them for myself.” He submitted the written confession. The prefect said, “The wretch was indeed tempted by wealth. There is no more to discuss. Bring a cangue, fasten it on him, and commit him to prison.” The jailers brought a long cangue, fastened it around Wu Song’s neck, and took him down to be confined in the condemned prisoners’ jail. p.src: Meanwhile, word of the affair reached Shi En, who hurried into the city to consult his father. The old prison superintendent said, “It is plain that Instructor Zhang is avenging Jiang the Gate God. He has bribed Commandant Zhang and devised this scheme to frame Wu Song. He must have sent men to bribe everyone from top to bottom. Having accepted his favors and money, they will refuse to hear Wu Song’s defense and will surely seek to take his life. Yet now that I think it over, his offense should not merit death. If we can only buy the favor of the wardens and jailers of the two prisons, we should be able to preserve his life. Once he is out, we can make other plans.” Shi En said, “The chief jailer presently in charge is a man named Kang, and he and I are on the closest of terms. Should I not go and appeal to him?” The old superintendent replied, “He landed in this lawsuit on your account. If you do not go to save him, what are you waiting for?” Taking one or two hundred taels of silver, Shi En went straight to Chief Jailer Kang’s house, but Kang was still at the prison and had not returned. Shi En asked Kang’s household to send someone to the prison and inform him. Before long, Chief Jailer Kang returned and met with Shi En. Shi En related the whole affair to him in detail. Chief Jailer Kang replied, “I will hide nothing from you, elder brother. Commandant Zhang and Instructor Zhang share the same surname and have sworn brotherhood with each other. Jiang the Gate God is now hiding in Instructor Zhang’s house. He persuaded the instructor to bribe Commandant Zhang, and together they devised this scheme. Everyone involved, high and low, was bribed by Jiang the Gate God, and we too accepted his money. In the court, the prefect has thrown his full support behind them and is determined to finish Wu Song off. Only Clerk Ye, who handles the case, refuses to consent, and for that reason they have not dared kill him. Clerk Ye is loyal, upright, and devoted to justice. He will not harm an innocent man, and thanks to him Wu Song has not yet suffered the worst. Now that I have heard what you say, Brother Shi, leave everything inside the prison to me; I shall look after him myself. I will go at once and ease his confinement, and henceforth I shall not let him suffer in the least. You must quickly send someone to appeal to Clerk Ye alone, urging him to pass sentence and send Wu Song away as soon as possible. That will save his life.” Shi En produced one hundred taels of silver and offered them to Chief Jailer Kang. Chief Jailer Kang would not accept it at first. Only after refusing it repeatedly did he finally take it.

p.src: Shi En took his leave and returned straight to the prison camp. There he found an acquaintance of Clerk Ye, gave him one hundred taels of silver, and begged him to press for a swift decision in the case. Clerk Ye already knew that Wu Song was a gallant man and had himself intended to protect him, so he had drafted the case papers with room for leniency. But the prefect, having accepted Commandant Zhang’s bribe and request, refused to deal leniently with him. The investigation found Wu Song guilty of stealing another man’s property, but that offense did not merit death. Thus the two sides kept delaying matters, while the prefect’s faction sought only to have him killed in prison. Now Clerk Ye had also received these hundred taels and knew that Wu Song had been falsely accused. He therefore revised the entire file to make the charges lighter, clearing Wu Song of everything he could, and waited only for the statutory period to expire before judgment was passed. p.src: The next day, Shi En prepared an abundant and complete spread of wine and food. He asked Chief Jailer Kang to conduct him straight into the great prison, where he visited Wu Song and brought him a meal. By then, Chief Jailer Kang had already taken Wu Song under his protection and relaxed all the rigors of his confinement. Shi En also took out twenty or thirty taels of silver and distributed them among the lesser jailers. After serving Wu Song wine and food, Shi En whispered in his ear, “This case is plainly Commandant Zhang’s attempt to avenge Jiang the Gate God by framing you, elder brother. Set your mind at ease for now, and do not worry. I have already sent someone to reach an understanding with Clerk Ye, and he is most willing to protect you. Wait until the term expires and he sentences you to leave this place; then we shall decide what to do next.” Now that his confinement had been eased, Wu Song had already conceived the idea of escaping from prison. But after hearing Shi En’s words, he abandoned the thought. Having comforted Wu Song in prison, Shi En returned to the prison camp. Two days later, Shi En again prepared wine, food, and money, and once more asked Chief Jailer Kang to conduct him into the prison to speak with Wu Song. When they met, Shi En entertained him with wine and food. He also distributed some small pieces of silver among the others as drinking money. After returning home, he again enlisted people to spend money at every level, urging the officials to hasten and arrange the documents. Several days later, Shi En again prepared wine and meat and made several garments. Once more he asked Chief Jailer Kang to assist and conduct him into the prison, where he treated everyone to wine and bought their favor so that they would care for Wu Song. He had Wu Song change into fresh clothes and partake of the wine and food. As he came and went, he grew familiar with them all; over the course of several days, Shi En visited the great prison three times. But unexpectedly, one of Instructor Zhang’s trusted men saw him and went back to report it. Instructor Zhang then went and told Commandant Zhang what had happened. Commandant Zhang again sent someone with gold and silks for the prefect and had the matter explained to him. The prefect was a corrupt official. Once he had accepted the bribe, he sent men down to the prison repeatedly to make inspections. Whenever they saw an unauthorized visitor, they were to arrest and question him. When Shi En learned of this, he no longer dared visit Wu Song. Wu Song, however, remained under the personal care of Chief Jailer Kang and the lesser jailers. From then on, Shi En could only go morning and evening to Chief Jailer Kang’s house to ask for news, and thus he kept informed of every development. But no more need be said of that.

p.src: In this way, nearly two months passed. Clerk Ye, who handled the case, argued forcefully on Wu Song’s behalf and explained the true circumstances to the prefect at every opportunity. Only then did the prefect learn that Commandant Zhang had accepted a considerable sum of silver from Jiang the Gate God and conspired with Instructor Zhang to devise a plot against Wu Song. He thought to himself, “You pocketed the silver, yet you expect me to kill a man for you!” After that, he lost all enthusiasm for the matter and ceased troubling himself over it.

p.src: When the sixty-day term finally expired, Wu Song was brought out of prison, and his cangue was opened before the court. Clerk Ye, who handled the case, read out the confession and proposed the sentence: twenty strokes across the back and penal exile to the Enzhou prison fortress, while the goods originally alleged stolen were to be returned to their owner. Commandant Zhang had no choice but to send a servant to claim the alleged stolen goods before the authorities. There in court, Wu Song was sentenced to twenty strokes across the back and branded with the convict’s mark. A seven-and-a-half-catty iron-plated, round-headed cangue was nailed upon him; an official writ was issued, and two strong constables were assigned to escort him under guard, with a fixed date set for departure. The two constables received the warrant, took custody of Wu Song, and immediately set out from the Mengzhou courthouse. In fact, when Wu Song received the sentence of the rod, the old prison superintendent had already spent money to smooth matters over; Clerk Ye also protected him, and the prefect knew that he had been framed and therefore did not have him struck too heavily. Thus the blows he received were light.

p.src: Wu Song swallowed his anger, put on the traveling cangue, and left the city with the two escorts guarding him from behind. After they had gone a little over a li, Shi En emerged from a tavern beside the highway and said to Wu Song, “I have been waiting here especially for you.” When Wu Song looked at him, he saw that Shi En’s head was bandaged again and his arm hung in a sling. Wu Song asked, “I have not seen you for some time. How did you come to look like this again?” Shi En replied, “To tell you the truth, brother: after I visited you three times in prison, the prefect learned of it and repeatedly sent men down to inspect the jail. Commandant Zhang also stationed men on both sides of the prison gate to keep watch. So I could no longer enter the jail to visit you and could only go to Warden Kang’s house for news. Half a month ago, while I was in my tavern at the Forest of Delight, that scoundrel Jiang the Door God came again with a band of soldiers and started a fight. They gave me another savage beating and forced me to find someone to plead and apologize for me. Then he seized the tavern again, and I had to hand all its furnishings back to him as before. I was still at home recovering when I heard today that you had been sentenced to exile in Enzhou. I have brought two padded garments for you to wear on the road. I have also cooked two geese. Please eat a few pieces before you go.” Shi En invited the two escorts into the tavern, but they refused to enter and began snarling, “Wu Song is a condemned rogue. If we were to eat your food and drink, there would surely be trouble with the authorities tomorrow. If you do not want a beating, clear off at once.” Seeing that persuasion was useless, Shi En took out a little over ten taels of silver and offered it to the two escorts. But the two scoundrels would not accept it. Seething with anger, they merely urged Wu Song to get moving. Shi En ordered two bowls of wine and had Wu Song drink them. He tied a bundle around Wu Song’s waist and hung the two cooked geese from his cangue. Then he whispered in Wu Song’s ear, “The bundle contains two padded garments and a kerchief full of small silver pieces for your traveling expenses. There are also two pairs of plaited hemp sandals inside. But you must be very much on your guard along the road. Those two villains mean you no good.” Wu Song nodded. “You need not tell me. I have already understood. Even if two more came, I would not fear them. Go home and tend your wounds. Set your mind at ease. I know how to deal with this.” Shi En bowed farewell to Wu Song and departed in tears. No more need be said of him.

Shi En ordered two bowls of wine and had Wu Song drink them. He tied a bundle around Wu Song’s waist and hung the two cooked geese from his cangue.
Then he whispered in Wu Song’s ear, “The bundle contains two padded garments and a kerchief full of small silver pieces for your traveling expenses.
There are also two pairs of plaited hemp sandals inside.
But you must be very much on your guard along the road. Those two villains mean you no good.”
Wu Song nodded. “You need not tell me. I have already understood.
Even if two more came, I would not fear them.
Go home and tend your wounds.
Set your mind at ease. I know how to deal with this.”
Shi En bowed farewell to Wu Song and departed in tears. No more need be said of him.

p.src: Wu Song set out with the two escorts. Before they had gone several li, the escorts whispered to each other, “Those two have not appeared.” Hearing them, Wu Song thought privately and sneered, “Damn your luck! So those bastards mean to ambush your master!” Wu Song’s right hand had been nailed fast to the traveling cangue, but his left hand remained free. He took one of the cooked geese down from the cangue and ate away, paying no attention to the two escorts. After another four or five li, he took down the other goose, gripped it in his right hand, tore pieces off with his left, and continued eating. Within another five li, he had finished both cooked geese. When they were some eight or nine li from the city, two men could be seen waiting ahead beside the road, each carrying a long-handled saber and wearing a waist saber. When they saw the escorts bringing Wu Song, they joined them and walked along. Wu Song saw the two escorts exchange winks and secret signals with the two men carrying long-handled sabers. Wu Song had noticed it at once and was now almost certain something was amiss, but he kept it to himself and pretended to see nothing.

p.src: After walking only a few more li, they came to a broad and shimmering fishing inlet, surrounded on every side by wild creeks and wide rivers. The five men reached a broad plank bridge at the edge of the inlet. On an archway stood a plaque bearing the three characters “Flying Cloud Pool.” On seeing it, Wu Song deliberately asked, “What is this place called?” The two escorts replied, “You are not blind. Surely you can see ‘Flying Cloud Pool’ written on the plaque beside the bridge.” Wu Song stopped. “I need to relieve myself.” The two men carrying long-handled sabers stepped closer, but Wu Song suddenly shouted, “Down you go!” His flying kick struck one squarely and sent him somersaulting into the water. The other hurriedly tried to turn, but Wu Song’s right foot was already upon him, and with a splash he too went into the water. The two escorts panicked and ran down from the bridge. Wu Song roared, “Where do you think you’re going?” With a single wrench he snapped the cangue in two and chased them down the bridge. Of the two, one had already collapsed from fright. Wu Song rushed forward and felled the fleeing man with a single punch to the back. He picked up a long-handled saber beside the water, caught him, and stabbed him several times, killing him on the spot. Then he turned back and stabbed the man who had collapsed several times as well. The two men who had been kicked into the water had just struggled to their feet and were about to flee. Wu Song pursued them and cut one down, then closed on the other, seized him by the hair, and shouted, “Tell me the truth, you scoundrel, and I will spare your life!” The man said, “We two are disciples of Jiang the Door God. Our master and Drillmaster Zhang devised this plan and sent us to assist the prisoner escorts so that together we might kill you, good sir.” Wu Song asked, “Where is your master, Jiang the Door God, now?” The man replied, “When I left, he and Drillmaster Zhang were drinking in the Mandarin Ducks Tower in the rear hall of Commandant Zhang’s residence, waiting especially for our report.” Wu Song said, “So that is how it was. Then I cannot spare you after all.” His hand rose and his saber fell, killing the man as well. He unfastened the man’s waist saber, chose the better weapon, and strapped it on. Then he hurled both corpses into the inlet. Fearing that the other two might not be dead, he raised the long-handled saber and stabbed each of them several more times. He stood on the bridge looking on for a while and thought, “Though I have killed these four villains, how can I vent my hatred unless I also kill Commandant Zhang, Drillmaster Zhang, and Jiang the Door God?” Holding the long-handled saber, he hesitated for some time. Then a thought came to him, and he headed straight back toward Mengzhou city.

p.src: Because of this deed, Wu Song was destined to slay several greedy villains and vent his bitter wrath. Deep in the painted hall, corpses would cover the floor; amid the glow of red candles, blood would fill the tower. As for what came of Wu Song’s return to Mengzhou city, listen to the explanation in the next chapter.
